OUR route publishes to a MULTI-COLUMN fp32 bank and reads the deepest committed column, same LOGICAL state, intentionally higher precision; the seam (if any) would be WHICH-COLUMN, and that is verified correct. NATIVE (vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_utils.py): get_conv_copy_spec/get_temporal_copy_spec :264-284 take num_accepted_tokens with documented Range 1..1+num_speculative_tokens (:259-260, native COUNTS the committed/bonus token, 1-based) and slice the running slot at column num_accepted_tokens-1 (:272 state[src_block_id, num_accepted_tokens-1:]). Native GDN spec verify (vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn_linear_attn.py:984-1005, causal_conv1d_update num_accepted_tokens=num_accepted_tokens, conv_state_indices=spec_state_indices_tensor[:,0]) rolls the post-accept state within the request own spec slot; the next iteration re-reads via spec_initial_state_indices, one durable slot per request, bf16, in-place. OURS: instead of one rolling slot, the committer replay re-executes the accepted path on the identical _gdn_node_step body (fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:674-688) and publishes each accepted token post-state to its OWN fp32 bank LINEAR column (:699-706); the next forward h0 reads column clamp(num_accepted-1,0) (:443-448). Both designs land the next forward h0 on the state after the deepest accepted token and both use the identical num_accepted-1 column offset. The differences vs native, (a) multi fp32 columns vs one bf16 slot, (b) replay re-execution vs in-place roll, are the INTENTIONAL higher-precision design (our fp32 state is deliberately MORE precise than native bf16 handoff), NOT a wiring divergence. There is no column-convention mismatch: native 1-based num_accepted_tokens with -1 offset equals our best_lcp with -1 clamp, both selecting the deepest-accepted state. Per the reward-hack note, aligning to native lossy bf16 handoff would be WRONG; the only thing to verify is the which-column wiring, which the A1 trace confirms is correct.

read.whatAtL56NotScan: SUBST_V2's "L56 carrier" is NOT a broken L56 op — it is a REFERENCE-PATH confound. SUBST_V2 measured (and spliced) vs the NO-SPEC SEQUENTIAL RANK-1 DECODE oracle (`fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode`, num_tokens=1, single row — native /tmp/vllm_live_019/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn_linear_attn.py:1295; confirmed in the raw: "no-spec sequential rank-1 DECODE whose FINAL decoded row is the next-token"). The tree-verify forward uses a DIFFERENT native kernel, `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` (gdn_linear_attn.py:1119 spec branch / :1165 decode branch). The BV A/B (FR13_BV_GEOMETRY_NOT_THE_SEAM, 2026-06-14, D16=D32=0.0 at N_PAD=1 and 16) proved OUR scan is bit-exact to NATIVE TREE-VERIFY at all geometries — but SUBST_V2 compared to native DECODE. "Matches native-tree-verify" != "matches no-spec-decode" (this is exactly the reconciliation in FR13_TREEVERIFY_SEAM_SCAN_BIND lines 27-32 and FR13_BV_GEOMETRY lines 33-36). L56 = the FIRST linear_attention/GDN block right after full_attn L55 (full_attention_interval=4 -> full-attn at {3,7,...,55,59,63}; qwen3_next.py:410/415 layer_type dispatch). What "diverges" at L56 given a clean L55 input is the tree-verify-forward's recurrently-built GDN state realization vs the recurrent-decode oracle's — a path-vs-path realization difference (~1 bf16 ULP/node, FR13_DIFFUSE_GDN_EXPLAINED), NOT a single L56 op. Every per-forward L56 GDN sub-op matches its native counterpart: conv tap bf16-rounded matches native (FR13_BF16_FP32_SEAM lines 8-18, causal_conv1d.py:1044), scan matches native tree-verify (BV A/B 0.0), gate=RMSNormGated and o_proj=out_proj are UNCHANGED native module calls (gdn_linear_attn.py:343 RMSNormGated norm_before_gate=True, :351 out_proj). So splice@[55]-still-diverges = L56 re-creating, on a clean input, the SAME tree-verify-vs-sequential-decode realization gap that this path always carries — it registers FIRST at L56 because L55 is the deep full_attn whose output feeds L56 (qwen3_next.py:405/407 input_layernorm + residual), making L56 the layer where the accumulated path difference first crosses pos21's modest ~0.5-logit verify-forward margin.
